steps.message:
# Diagnose and repair the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system evaluates your repaired workspace itself after you finish
(see below); anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap,
non-training checks are fine.

**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages,
or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and
repair using only what is staged locally.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Verdict** — healthy or unhealthy, with the evidence that decides it.
2. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
3. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
4. **Expected effect** — which behavior the fix should change and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system runs a task-specific verifier against
your repaired workspace. There is no training rerun and no LLM judge — the
verifier itself is the whole evaluation. It selects, for each held-out
episode, the rule the training bridge would select (by scenario and task
index) from

```text
data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl
```

in your repaired workspace, and replays the episode through that rule. The
score is the fraction of episodes classified correctly. Every original entry
in the rule file must remain present and parseable, and a file that was
wholesale-replaced, truncated, or corrupted makes the run ungradeable and
scores 0. Do not modify the preserved evidence under `logs/`, and do not
modify any evaluation, oracle, or verifier file. Otherwise the run is scored 0.
I'll start by exploring the workspace structure.

43	def immutable_revision(value):
44	    if not value or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", value):
45	        raise ValueError("Downloads require a 40-character immutable HF commit SHA")
46	    return value

49	def download_data(repo_id, revision):
50	    from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
51	    immutable_revision(revision)
52	    snapshot = Path(snapshot_download(repo_id, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision, token=hub_token(),
53	                                     allow_patterns=["rl/*", "runtime/*", "manifest.json"]))
54	    root = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
55	    mapping = [(snapshot / "rl/train.parquet", root / "verl/train.parquet"),
56	               (snapshot / "rl/validation.parquet", root / "verl/test.parquet")]
57	    names = ["gen_db", "gen_envs", "gen_sample", "gen_tasks", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
58	    mapping += [(snapshot / "runtime" / (name + ".jsonl"), root / (name + ".jsonl")) for name in names]
59	    for source, target in mapping:
60	        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
61	        if not target.exists():
62	            shutil.copy2(source, target)
63	    manifest = json.loads((ROOT.parent / "environment/data_manifest.json").read_text())
64	    expected = {item["path"]: item for item in manifest["files"]}
65	    for _, target in mapping:
66	        item = expected[target.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()]
67	        with target.open("rb") as stream:
68	            digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
69	        if target.stat().st_size != item["bytes"] or digest != item["sha256"]:
70	            raise ValueError("Restored data differs from historical inputs: " + target.name)

117	def check(config):
118	    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
119	    data = Path(config.env.awm.data_root)
120	    required = ["gen_tasks", "gen_envs", "gen_db", "gen_sample", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
121	    records = {}
122	    for name in required:
123	        with (data / f"{name}.jsonl").open() as stream:
124	            records[name] = [json.loads(line) for line in stream if line.strip()]
125	    scenarios = {name: {row["scenario"] for row in rows} for name, rows in records.items()}
126	    tasks = {row["scenario"]: row["tasks"] for row in records["gen_tasks"]}
127	    splits = {}
128	    keys = {}
129	    for split in ("train", "test"):
130	        rows = pq.read_table(data / f"verl/{split}.parquet").to_pylist()
131	        keys[split] = set()
132	        for row in rows:
133	            item = row["env_kwargs"]
134	            scenario, index = item["scenario"], item["task_idx"]
135	            assert item["task"] == tasks[scenario][index], (scenario, index)
136	            assert all(scenario in values for values in scenarios.values()), scenario
137	            keys[split].add((scenario, index))
138	        assert len(keys[split]) == len(rows), f"duplicate {split} task"
139	        splits[split] = rows
140	    assert not keys["train"] & keys["test"], "train/test overlap"
141	    assert len(keys["train"] | keys["test"]) == sum(len(t) for t in tasks.values())
142	    model = Path(config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path)
143	    for filename in ("config.json", "tokenizer.json", "tokenizer_config.json"):
144	        if not (model / filename).is_file():
145	            raise FileNotFoundError(model / filename)
146	    if not list(model.glob("*.safetensors")) and not list(model.glob("pytorch_model*.bin")):
147	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Model weights not found in {model}")
148	    if not Path(config.env.awm.python).is_file():
149	        raise FileNotFoundError(config.env.awm.python)
150	    return splits, {"split_rows": {k: len(v) for k, v in splits.items()},
151	                    "scenario_counts": {k: len(v) for k, v in scenarios.items()},
152	                    "task_alignment": "passed", "train_test_overlap": 0,
153	                    "model_config_and_weights_present": True}

156	def smoke(config, output, splits):
157	    # Load the packaged environment directly, without importing unrelated envs.
158	    path = ROOT / "idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/envs.py"
159	    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("packaged_awm_env", path)
160	    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
161	    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
162	    selected = []
163	    seen = set()
164	    for rows in (splits["train"], splits["test"], splits["train"][1:]):
165	        for row in rows:
166	            item = row["env_kwargs"]
167	            if item["scenario"] not in seen:
168	                selected.append(item)
169	                seen.add(item["scenario"])

171	    env = module.AWMMCPVectorEnv(len(selected), 1, config.env)
172	    try:
173	        tasks, _ = env.reset(selected)
174	        observations, _, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "list_tools", "arguments": None}] * len(selected))
175	        for item, observation, done, info in zip(selected, observations, dones, infos):
176	            if done or info.get("reward_type") == "environment_error":
177	                raise RuntimeError(f"Environment startup failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
178	            assert observation, "empty tool listing"
179	        _, rewards, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "final", "content": "Smoke test, no task actions performed."}] * len(selected))
180	        assert all(dones), "final action did not terminate"
181	        for item, info in zip(selected, infos):
182	            if info.get("reward_type") in {"environment_error", "judge_error", "server_error"}:
183	                raise RuntimeError(f"Verifier failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
184	        return [{"scenario": item["scenario"], "task_idx": item["task_idx"],
185	                 "reset": bool(task), "list_tools": "passed", "final": "passed",
186	                 "reward": reward, "reward_type": info.get("reward_type")}
187	                for item, task, reward, info in zip(selected, tasks, rewards, infos)]
188	    finally:

201	    parser.add_argument("--output", default=str(ROOT / "reproduction" / datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")))

206	    args, overrides = parser.parse_known_args()

237	        env.setdefault("NCCL_P2P_DISABLE", "0")
238	        env.setdefault("TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT", "1")
239	        ray_root = os.environ.get("RAY_TMPDIR")
240	        env["RAY_TMPDIR"] = ray_root or str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"i4ray-{os.getpid()}")
241	        Path(env["RAY_TMPDIR"]).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
242	        for name in ("http_proxy", "https_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "all_proxy", "ALL_PROXY"):
243	            env.pop(name, None)
244	        command = [sys.executable, "-m", "verl.trainer.main_ppo", "--config-path", str(output), "--config-name", "config"]
245	        command += ["hydra.run.dir=" + str(output)]
246	        if args.config_only:

253	        print(f"Exit code: {result.returncode}; combined stdout/stderr: {log_path}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prepare a relocated recorded config, check inputs, or launch the issue run."""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import runpy
import re
import shutil
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from omegaconf import OmegaConf

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "idea_source"))


def runtime_defaults():
    """Optional machine-local paths, never credentials or historical evidence."""
    path = ROOT.parent / "runtime.local.json"
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    values = json.loads(path.read_text())
    unknown = set(values) - {"awm_python", "model_path", "model_revision", "dataset_revision"}
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported runtime.local.json keys: " + ", ".join(sorted(unknown)))
    return values


def hub_token():
    if os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN"):
        return os.environ["HF_TOKEN"]
    path = os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN_PATH")
    return Path(path).read_text().strip() if path else None


def immutable_revision(value):
    if not value or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", value):
        raise ValueError("Downloads require a 40-character immutable HF commit SHA")
    return value


def download_data(repo_id, revision):
    from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
    immutable_revision(revision)
    snapshot = Path(snapshot_download(repo_id, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision, token=hub_token(),
                                     allow_patterns=["rl/*", "runtime/*", "manifest.json"]))
    root = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
    mapping = [(snapshot / "rl/train.parquet", root / "verl/train.parquet"),
               (snapshot / "rl/validation.parquet", root / "verl/test.parquet")]
    names = ["gen_db", "gen_envs", "gen_sample", "gen_tasks", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
    mapping += [(snapshot / "runtime" / (name + ".jsonl"), root / (name + ".jsonl")) for name in names]
    for source, target in mapping:
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists():
            shutil.copy2(source, target)
    manifest = json.loads((ROOT.parent / "environment/data_manifest.json").read_text())
    expected = {item["path"]: item for item in manifest["files"]}
    for _, target in mapping:
        item = expected[target.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()]
        with target.open("rb") as stream:
            digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
        if target.stat().st_size != item["bytes"] or digest != item["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Restored data differs from historical inputs: " + target.name)


def prepare(args):
    original = OmegaConf.load(ROOT / "config/.hydra/config.yaml")
    config = OmegaConf.create(OmegaConf.to_container(original, resolve=False))
    data = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
    output = Path(args.output).absolute()
    python = Path(args.awm_python).absolute()
    model = Path(args.model_path).expanduser()
    if not model.is_dir():
        if model.is_absolute() or args.model_path.startswith("."):
            raise FileNotFoundError(model)
        immutable_revision(args.model_revision)
        from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
        model = Path(snapshot_download(args.model_path, revision=args.model_revision, token=hub_token(),
                                       local_dir=ROOT / "models/IDEA_sft"))
    model = model.absolute()
    config.data.train_files = str(data / "verl/train.parquet")
    config.data.val_files = str(data / "verl/test.parquet")
    config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path = str(model)
    config.env.awm.root = str(ROOT / "awm_source")
    config.env.awm.python = str(python)
    config.env.awm.data_root = str(data)
    config.env.awm.work_root = str(output / "awm_runtime")
    # Code rewards do not use a hosted judge; never carry a recorded credential
    # into a new config or console log.
    config.env.awm.judge_api_key = (
        os.environ.get("AWM_JUDGE_API_KEY", "EMPTY")
        if config.env.awm.reward_mode == "sql" else "EMPTY"
    )
    if config.env.awm.reward_mode == "sql" and config.env.awm.judge_api_key == "EMPTY":
        raise RuntimeError("SQL reward mode requires AWM_JUDGE_API_KEY")
    for field, folder in (("analysis_dump_dir", "idea_analysis"),
                          ("augmented_observation_dump_dir", "idea_augmented_observations"),
                          ("state_group_dump_dir", "idea_state_group")):
        config.algorithm.seed[field] = str(output / folder)
    config.trainer.rollout_data_dir = str(output / "rollouts")
    config.trainer.default_local_dir = str(output / "checkpoints")
    config.trainer.resume_mode = "disable"
    config.trainer.resume_from_path = None
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OmegaConf.resolve(config)
    OmegaConf.save(config, output / "config.yaml")
    return config, output


def check(config):
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    data = Path(config.env.awm.data_root)
    required = ["gen_tasks", "gen_envs", "gen_db", "gen_sample", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
    records = {}
    for name in required:
        with (data / f"{name}.jsonl").open() as stream:
            records[name] = [json.loads(line) for line in stream if line.strip()]
    scenarios = {name: {row["scenario"] for row in rows} for name, rows in records.items()}
    tasks = {row["scenario"]: row["tasks"] for row in records["gen_tasks"]}
    splits = {}
    keys = {}
    for split in ("train", "test"):
        rows = pq.read_table(data / f"verl/{split}.parquet").to_pylist()
        keys[split] = set()
        for row in rows:
            item = row["env_kwargs"]
            scenario, index = item["scenario"], item["task_idx"]
            assert item["task"] == tasks[scenario][index], (scenario, index)
            assert all(scenario in values for values in scenarios.values()), scenario
            keys[split].add((scenario, index))
        assert len(keys[split]) == len(rows), f"duplicate {split} task"
        splits[split] = rows
    assert not keys["train"] & keys["test"], "train/test overlap"
    assert len(keys["train"] | keys["test"]) == sum(len(t) for t in tasks.values())
    model = Path(config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path)
    for filename in ("config.json", "tokenizer.json", "tokenizer_config.json"):
        if not (model / filename).is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(model / filename)
    if not list(model.glob("*.safetensors")) and not list(model.glob("pytorch_model*.bin")):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Model weights not found in {model}")
    if not Path(config.env.awm.python).is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(config.env.awm.python)
    return splits, {"split_rows": {k: len(v) for k, v in splits.items()},
                    "scenario_counts": {k: len(v) for k, v in scenarios.items()},
                    "task_alignment": "passed", "train_test_overlap": 0,
                    "model_config_and_weights_present": True}


def smoke(config, output, splits):
    # Load the packaged environment directly, without importing unrelated envs.
    path = ROOT / "idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/envs.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("packaged_awm_env", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for rows in (splits["train"], splits["test"], splits["train"][1:]):
        for row in rows:
            item = row["env_kwargs"]
            if item["scenario"] not in seen:
                selected.append(item)
                seen.add(item["scenario"])
                break
    env = module.AWMMCPVectorEnv(len(selected), 1, config.env)
    try:
        tasks, _ = env.reset(selected)
        observations, _, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "list_tools", "arguments": None}] * len(selected))
        for item, observation, done, info in zip(selected, observations, dones, infos):
            if done or info.get("reward_type") == "environment_error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Environment startup failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
            assert observation, "empty tool listing"
        _, rewards, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "final", "content": "Smoke test, no task actions performed."}] * len(selected))
        assert all(dones), "final action did not terminate"
        for item, info in zip(selected, infos):
            if info.get("reward_type") in {"environment_error", "judge_error", "server_error"}:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Verifier failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
        return [{"scenario": item["scenario"], "task_idx": item["task_idx"],
                 "reset": bool(task), "list_tools": "passed", "final": "passed",
                 "reward": reward, "reward_type": info.get("reward_type")}
                for item, task, reward, info in zip(selected, tasks, rewards, infos)]
    finally:
        env.close()


def main():
    defaults = runtime_defaults()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", default=os.environ.get("MODEL_PATH", defaults.get("model_path", "locaszzz/IDEA_sft")))
    parser.add_argument("--model-revision", default=os.environ.get("MODEL_REVISION", defaults.get("model_revision")))
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-revision", default=os.environ.get("DATASET_REVISION", defaults.get("dataset_revision")))
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-repo", default="locaszzz/IDEA_training_data")
    parser.add_argument("--download-data", action="store_true", help="Fetch RL/runtime inputs from the Hub dataset if absent; authenticate only if required")
    parser.add_argument("--awm-python", default=os.environ.get("AWM_PYTHON", defaults.get("awm_python", "/opt/awm/bin/python")))
    parser.add_argument("--output", default=str(ROOT / "reproduction" / datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")))
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="Test MCP startup, list_tools, and code verifier; no model inference")
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--train", action="store_true", help="Launch the recorded 200-step issue configuration; requires 8 free 80GB GPUs")
    mode.add_argument("--config-only", action="store_true", help="Also check Hydra composition without starting Ray or training")
    args, overrides = parser.parse_known_args()
    if overrides and not (args.train or args.config_only):
        parser.error("Hydra overrides require --train or --config-only")
    if args.download_data:
        download_data(args.dataset_repo, args.dataset_revision)
    if not Path(args.awm_python).is_file():
        parser.error("Set AWM_PYTHON or configure runtime.local.json with the separate AWM interpreter")
    config, output = prepare(args)
    splits, report = check(config)
    report["python"] = sys.executable
    report["scope"] = "input checks; NOT a completed training run"

Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

Zhaoyang Wang1, Canwen Xu2, Boyi Liu2, Yite Wang2, Siwei Han1,
Zhewei Yao2, Huaxiu Yao1, Yuxiong He2

1UNC-Chapel Hill   2Snowflake AI Research  

# Overview **AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning. Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline: 1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform") 2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements 3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend 4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space 5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model). # Resources Related resources are also available, please check: | Resource | Link | AgentWorldModel-1K

Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

Zhaoyang Wang1, Canwen Xu2, Boyi Liu2, Yite Wang2, Siwei Han1,
Zhewei Yao2, Huaxiu Yao1, Yuxiong He2

1UNC-Chapel Hill   2Snowflake AI Research  

# Overview **AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning. Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline: 1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform") 2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements 3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend 4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space 5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model). # Resources Related resources are also available, please check: | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | 📄 Paper | [📄 arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090) | | 💻 Code | [💻 Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model) | | 📦 AgentWorldModel-1K | [🤗 Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-4B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-8B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-14B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B) | # Dataset Files | File | #Entries | Description | |------|----------|-------------| | `gen_scenario.jsonl` | 1,000 | Synthesized scenario descriptions | | `gen_tasks.jsonl` | 1,000 | 10 user tasks per scenario | | `gen_db.jsonl` | 1,000 | Database schema definitions for each scenario | | `gen_sample.jsonl` | 1,000 | Sample data to populate the initial database state | | `gen_spec.jsonl` | 1,000 | API specifications for each scenario's interface | | `gen_envs.jsonl` | 1,000 | MCP environment code (FastAPI + MCP server) | | `gen_verifier.jsonl` | 10K | Verification code for code-augmented LLM-as-a-Judge | | `gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl` | 10K | Verification code for purely code-based Judge | # AgentWorldModel-1K

Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

Zhaoyang Wang1, Canwen Xu2, Boyi Liu2, Yite Wang2, Siwei Han1,
Zhewei Yao2, Huaxiu Yao1, Yuxiong He2

1UNC-Chapel Hill   2Snowflake AI Research  

# Overview **AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning. Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline: 1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform") 2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements 3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend 4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space 5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model). # Resources Related resources are also available, please check: | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | 📄 Paper | [📄 arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090) | | 💻 Code | [💻 Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model) | | 📦 AgentWorldModel-1K | [🤗 Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-4B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-8B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-14B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B) | # Dataset Files | File | #Entries | Description | |------|----------|-------------| | `gen_scenario.jsonl` | 1,000 | Synthesized scenario descriptions | | `gen_tasks.jsonl` | 1,000 | 10 user tasks per scenario | | `gen_db.jsonl` | 1,000 | Database schema definitions for each scenario | | `gen_sample.jsonl` | 1,000 | Sample data to populate the initial database state | | `gen_spec.jsonl` | 1,000 | API specifications for each scenario's interface | | `gen_envs.jsonl` | 1,000 | MCP environment code (FastAPI + MCP server) | | `gen_verifier.jsonl` | 10K | Verification code for code-augmented LLM-as-a-Judge | | `gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl` | 10K | Verification code for purely code-based Judge | # # Overview **AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning. Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline: 1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform") 2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements 3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend 4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space 5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model). # #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""JSON-lines bridge to Agent World Model's Python 3.12 MCP runtime."""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import shutil
import signal
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from awm.core.agent import MCPToolExecutor, format_tools_for_response, parse_call_tool_arguments
from awm.core.server import Config as ServerConfig, _prepare_database, start_server_process
from awm.core.verify import run_verifier, run_llm_judge
from awm.tools import find_scenario_entry, get_random_available_port, tools_jsonl_load


# Reward contract used by the AWM RL environment.  Unknown verifier/judge
# outcomes intentionally receive zero rather than being treated as failures.
REWARD_BY_TYPE = {
    "complete": 1.0,
    "completed": 1.0,
    "incomplete": 0.1,
    "partially_completed": 0.1,
    "partial": 0.1,
    # Pure-code verifiers use `others` for an unsuccessful completion check;
    # unsuccessful/unknown outcomes are agent/environment errors and receive
    # zero task reward.
    "others": 0.0,
    "agent_error": 0.0,
    "environment_error": 0.0,
    "server_error": 0.0,
    "judge_error": 0.0,
    "format_error": -1.0,
    "tool_not_found": -1.0,
    "invalid_args": -1.0,
}

# Judge labels that count as a successful / partial task outcome.  Terminal
# shaping below only rewrites these; environment/agent errors stay as-is.
_COMPLETE_TYPES = {"complete", "completed"}
_INCOMPLETE_TYPES = {"incomplete", "partially_completed", "partial"}
# Identical successful tool calls (same name + arguments) this many times in a
# row end the episode and run the verifier instead of letting the agent loop.
DEFAULT_REPEAT_SUCCESS_TERMINATE_K = 5


@dataclass
class Session:
    scenario: str
    task_idx: int
    task: str
    output_dir: str
    db_path: str
    server: object | None
    mcp: MCPToolExecutor | None
    tools_text: str
    verifier: dict
    steps: int = 0
    done: bool = False
    trajectory: list[dict] | None = None
    startup_error: str | None = None
    # Consecutive MCP service failures are tracked separately from malformed
    # model actions.  A repeated identical failure indicates an environment
    # problem rather than an agent error.
    last_mcp_error: str | None = None
    mcp_error_streak: int = 0
    last_success_call_key: str | None = None
    success_call_streak: int = 0


class Bridge:
    def __init__(self, config: dict):
        self.root = Path(config["awm_root"])
        self.data = Path(config["data_root"])
        self.max_steps = int(config["max_steps"])
        self.tool_timeout = float(config.get("tool_timeout", 60))
        self.reward_mode = str(config.get("reward_mode", "code")).lower()
        if self.reward_mode not in {"code", "sql"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported reward_mode: {self.reward_mode}; expected code or sql")
        self.judge_base_url = str(config.get("judge_base_url", ""))
        self.judge_api_key = str(config.get("judge_api_key", "EMPTY"))
        self.judge_model = str(config.get("judge_model", ""))
        self.judge_timeout = float(config.get("judge_timeout", 120))
        self.judge_max_retries = int(config.get("judge_max_retries", 3))
        self.judge_concurrency = min(10, max(1, int(config.get("judge_concurrency", 10))))
        self.judge_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.judge_concurrency)
        # Starting hundreds of MCP subprocesses at once can starve the
        # readiness probes and make otherwise healthy servers miss the window.
        self.startup_concurrency = max(1, int(config.get("startup_concurrency", 32)))
        self.startup_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.startup_concurrency)
        self.repeat_success_terminate_k = max(
            2, int(config.get("repeat_success_terminate_k", DEFAULT_REPEAT_SUCCESS_TERMINATE_K))
        )
        work_root = config.get("work_root")
        self.work_root = Path(work_root) if work_root else Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed_awm_"))
        self.work_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # Keep the complete hosted LLM-as-judge response independently of the
        # rollout tensors.  The trainer only propagates a subset of env info,
        # so this JSONL is the authoritative per-trajectory judge trace.
        self.judge_log_path = self.work_root / "llm_judge.jsonl"
        # The verifier reads these in the isolated AWM subprocess.
        os.environ["AWM_JUDGE_TIMEOUT"] = str(self.judge_timeout)
        os.environ["AWM_JUDGE_MAX_RETRIES"] = str(self.judge_max_retries)
        self.sessions: list[Session] = []
        verifier_file = "gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl" if self.reward_mode == "code" else "gen_verifier.jsonl"
        self.verifiers = tools_jsonl_load(str(self.data / verifier_file))

    def _record_judge(
        self,
        session: Session,
        reward_type: str,
        verifier_result: dict,
        judge_result: dict | None,
        shaped_reward_type: str | None = None,
        ended_with_final: bool | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Append one complete Judge decision to the bridge-owned JSONL log."""
        entry = {
            "timestamp": time.time(),
            "scenario": session.scenario,
            "task_idx": session.task_idx,
            "task": session.task,
            "steps": len(session.trajectory or []),
            "reward_type": reward_type,
            "verifier_result": verifier_result,
            "llm_judge": judge_result,
        }
        if shaped_reward_type is not None:
            entry["shaped_reward_type"] = shaped_reward_type
        if ended_with_final is not None:
            entry["ended_with_final"] = ended_with_final
        with self.judge_log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")

    async def _stop_server(self, proc):
        if proc is None:
            return
        try:
            pgid = os.getpgid(proc.pid)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pgid = None
        if pgid is not None:
            try:
                os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM)
                await asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait, 5)
            except Exception:
                pass
            # awm.core.server launches uvicorn through a shell; clean any group remnants.
            try:
                os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
        for pipe in (proc.stdout, proc.stderr):
            if pipe:
                pipe.close()

    async def close(self):
        await self.close_sessions()

    async def close_sessions(self):
        for session in self.sessions:
            proc = session.server
            await self._stop_server(proc)
        self.sessions = []

    async def _start_one(self, index: int, item: dict) -> Session:
        scenario = str(item["scenario"])
        task_idx = int(item["task_idx"])
        last_error = None
        for attempt in range(1, 4):
            output_dir = self.work_root / f"env_{index}"
            if output_dir.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(output_dir)
            output_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
            server = None
            try:
                server_config = ServerConfig(
                    scenario=scenario,
                    envs_load_path=str(self.data / "gen_envs.jsonl"),
                    db_schema_path=str(self.data / "gen_db.jsonl"),
                    sample_path=str(self.data / "gen_sample.jsonl"),
                    temp_server_path=str(output_dir / "server_runtime.py"),
                )
                db_path = _prepare_database(server_config, str(output_dir))
                port = get_random_available_port()
                server = start_server_process(
                    scenario, str(self.data / "gen_envs.jsonl"), db_path, port,
                    output_dir=str(output_dir), temp_server_path=server_config.temp_server_path,
                )
                ready = False
                for _ in range(120):
                    if server.poll() is not None:
                        break
                    try:
                        _reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
                        writer.close()
                        await writer.wait_closed()
                        ready = True
                        break
                    except OSError:
                        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
                if not ready:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"MCP server failed to start for {scenario} task {task_idx}")
                mcp = MCPToolExecutor(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/mcp", timeout=self.tool_timeout)
                tools = []
                for tool_attempt in range(10):
                    tools = await mcp.list_tools()
                    if any(tool.get("name") != "list_tools" for tool in tools):
                        break
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(0.5 * (tool_attempt + 1), 2.0))
                if not any(tool.get("name") != "list_tools" for tool in tools):
                    raise RuntimeError(f"MCP business tools did not register for {scenario} task {task_idx}")
                verifier = find_scenario_entry(self.verifiers, scenario, task_idx=task_idx)
                if not verifier:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Verifier not found for {scenario} task {task_idx}")
                return Session(
                    scenario=scenario, task_idx=task_idx, task=str(item["task"]),
                    output_dir=str(output_dir), db_path=db_path, server=server, mcp=mcp,
                    tools_text=format_tools_for_response(tools), verifier=verifier, trajectory=[],
                )
            except BaseException as exc:
                last_error = exc
                await self._stop_server(server)
                if attempt < 3:
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * attempt)

        # Keep this item in the vector so the rollout batch remains aligned.
        return Session(
            scenario=scenario, task_idx=task_idx, task=str(item["task"]),
            output_dir=str(self.work_root / f"env_{index}"), db_path="", server=None, mcp=None,
            tools_text="", verifier={}, done=True, trajectory=[],
            startup_error=f"MCP startup failed after 3 attempts: {last_error}",
        )

    async def reset(self, items: list[dict]) -> dict:
        await self.close()

        async def start_limited(index: int, item: dict):
            async with self.startup_semaphore:
                return await self._start_one(index, item)

        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *(start_limited(i, item) for i, item in enumerate(items)),
            return_exceptions=True,
        )
        self.sessions = [result for result in results if isinstance(result, Session)]
        errors = [result for result in results if isinstance(result, BaseException)]
        if errors:
            # Unexpected bridge-level errors are still fatal; individual task
            # startup failures are represented by placeholder sessions above.
            await self.close()
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to start {len(errors)} AWM environment(s): {errors[0]}")
        return {"tasks": [session.task for session in self.sessions]}

    async def _verify(self, session: Session, final_answer: str) -> tuple[float, dict, dict, dict | None, str]:
        reward_type, details = run_verifier(
            session.verifier, self.reward_mode,
            str(Path(session.output_dir) / "initial.db"), session.db_path, final_answer,
        )
        judge_result = None
        if self.reward_mode == "sql" and reward_type != "judge_error":
            if not self.judge_base_url or not self.judge_model:
                reward_type = "judge_error"
                judge_result = {"error": "sql reward mode requires judge_base_url and judge_model"}
            else:
                async with self.judge_semaphore:
                    reward_type, judge_result = await run_llm_judge(
                        task=session.task, verifier_result=details,
                        llm_base_url=self.judge_base_url, llm_api_key=self.judge_api_key,
                        llm_model=self.judge_model, trajectory=session.trajectory or [],
                    )
        info = {"reward_type": reward_type, "verify_result": details}
        if judge_result is not None:
            info["llm_judge"] = judge_result
        normalized_type = str(reward_type).strip().lower().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
        return REWARD_BY_TYPE.get(normalized_type, 0.0), info, details, judge_result, reward_type

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_reward_type(reward_type: str | None) -> str:
        return str(reward_type or "").strip().lower().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")

    @staticmethod
    def _success_call_key(name: str, tool_name: str | None, tool_args) -> str | None:
        """Stable identity for a successful list_tools / call_tool action."""
        if name == "list_tools":
            return "list_tools"
        if name != "call_tool" or not tool_name:
            return None
        try:
            args_repr = json.dumps(tool_args, sort_keys=True, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)
        except TypeError:
            args_repr = str(tool_args)
        return f"call_tool:{tool_name}:{args_repr}"

    def _shape_terminal_reward(self, name: str, reward: float, verify_info: dict) -> tuple[float, dict]:
        """Rewrite complete/incomplete when the episode did not end on a final answer.

        complete + last action is still a tool call -> 0.5
        incomplete + no final answer -> -1.0
        Environment / judge / format errors are left unchanged.
        """
        if name == "final":
            return reward, verify_info
        original = self._normalize_reward_type(verify_info.get("reward_type"))
        if original in _COMPLETE_TYPES:
            verify_info = {
                **verify_info,
                "judge_reward_type": original,
                "reward_type": "complete_no_final",
            }
            return 0.5, verify_info
        if original in _INCOMPLETE_TYPES:
            verify_info = {
                **verify_info,
                "judge_reward_type": original,
                "reward_type": "incomplete_no_final",
            }
            return -1.0, verify_info
        return reward, verify_info

    async def _step_one(self, session: Session, action: dict) -> dict:
        if session.startup_error:
            return {
                "observation": f"Environment unavailable: {session.startup_error}",
                "reward": 0.0, "done": True, "action_valid": True,
                "reward_type": "environment_error",
            }
        if session.done:
            return {"observation": "", "reward": 0.0, "done": True}
        session.steps += 1
        name = action.get("name")
        # A malformed tool call is a format failure: stop immediately and
        # assign the contract's -1.0 step reward.  It must not continue until
        # max_steps or enter task-level verification.
        format_failure = name in {"invalid", None} or name not in {"final", "list_tools", "call_tool", "invalid"}
        done = name == "final" or session.steps >= self.max_steps or format_failure
        response = ""
        action_valid = True
        action_error = None
        mcp_error_key = None
        tool_name, tool_args = None, None
        if name == "final":
            # Plain final answers are valid terminal actions.  The content is
            # passed to the verifier below.
            response = str(action.get("content", ""))
        elif name == "list_tools":
            response = session.tools_text
        elif name == "call_tool":
            try:
                tool_name, tool_args = parse_call_tool_arguments(action.get("arguments"))
            except Exception:
                tool_name, tool_args = None, None
            if not tool_name:
                response = "Error: call_tool requires tool_name and JSON arguments"
                action_valid = False
                action_error = "invalid_args"
            else:
                try:
                    response = await session.mcp.call_tool(tool_name, tool_args)
                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                    response = f"Error: MCP tool call timed out after {self.tool_timeout}s"
                    action_valid = False
                    mcp_error_key = response
                except Exception as exc:
                    response = f"Error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
                    action_valid = False
                    mcp_error_key = response
                else:
                    # Some MCP implementations return an error payload as a
                    # string instead of raising.  Treat those responses as
                    # service errors too, while leaving ordinary tool output
                    # untouched.
                    if isinstance(response, str) and response.startswith("Error:"):
                        action_valid = False
                        mcp_error_key = response
        elif name == "invalid":
            response = "Error: output one valid <tool_call> block, or a plain final answer."
            action_valid = False
            action_error = "format_error"
        else:
            action_valid = False
            action_error = "format_error"

        if mcp_error_key is not None:
            if session.last_mcp_error == mcp_error_key:
                session.mcp_error_streak += 1
            else:
                session.last_mcp_error = mcp_error_key
                session.mcp_error_streak = 1
            # Two consecutive identical MCP failures are treated as an
            # environment failure.  Do not attribute this to the agent.
            if session.mcp_error_streak >= 2:
                action_error = "environment_error"
                done = True
            session.last_success_call_key = None
            session.success_call_streak = 0
        else:
            session.last_mcp_error = None
            session.mcp_error_streak = 0

        # Malformed arguments and invalid output remain terminal agent errors.
        if action_error is not None and action_error != "environment_error":
            done = True
            session.last_success_call_key = None
            session.success_call_streak = 0

        # Identical successful tool calls in a row are treated as looping:
        # stop and send the trajectory to the verifier instead of burning
        # the remaining budget on the same call.  MCP errors are not
        # successful calls and must not count toward this streak.
        if action_error is None and mcp_error_key is None and name in {"list_tools", "call_tool"}:
            call_key = self._success_call_key(name, tool_name, tool_args)
            if call_key and call_key == session.last_success_call_key:
                session.success_call_streak += 1
            else:
                session.last_success_call_key = call_key
                session.success_call_streak = 1
            if session.success_call_streak >= self.repeat_success_terminate_k:
                done = True
        elif action_error is None and mcp_error_key is None:
            session.last_success_call_key = None
            session.success_call_streak = 0

        session.trajectory.append({
            "iteration": session.steps, "role": "assistant",
            "content": str(action.get("content", "")),
            "tool_calls": [action] if name in {"list_tools", "call_tool", "invalid"} else [],
            "tool_response": {"content": response},
        })

        # Only normally completed trajectories are sent to the task verifier.
        # Format failures are terminal immediately and bypass task judging.
        reward = 0.0

async def main() -> None:
    config = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
    bridge = Bridge(config)
    try:
        for line in sys.stdin:
            try:
                request = json.loads(line)
                command = request.pop("command")
                if command == "reset":
                    result = await bridge.reset(request["items"])
                elif command == "step":
                    result = await bridge.step(request["actions"])
                elif command == "close_sessions":

                print(json.dumps({"ok": True, **result}, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)

            except Exception as exc:
                print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}), flush=True)

import json, collections, sys
root="/workspace/data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
def load(name):
    with open(f"{root}/{name}.jsonl") as f:

T=load("gen_tasks")

# duplicates by scenario/task_idx
cnt=collections.Counter((v.get("scenario"), v.get("task_idx")) for v in V)
dups={k:c for k,c in cnt.items() if c>1}
print("unique keys", len(cnt), "dup keys", len(dups), "extra entries", len(V)-len(cnt))
for k in list(dups)[:20]:
    entries=[v for v in V if (v.get("scenario"),v.get("task_idx"))==k]
    print("DUP", k, "count", len(entries))
    for e in entries:
        print("   scenario_raw=",repr(e.get("scenario")), "task_idx=",repr(e.get("task_idx")), "task=",repr(e.get("task"))[:120], "codelen=",len(e.get("verification",{}).get("code","")))
# task idx range
idxs=sorted(set(v.get("task_idx") for v in V))
print("task_idx values", idxs[:20], "n=",len(idxs))

scen_v=set(v.get("scenario") for v in V)

print("scen verifier",len(scen_v),"tasks",len(scen_t),"missing in verifier",len(scen_t-scen_v),"extra",len(scen_v-scen_t))
# tasks count per scenario
taskmap={t["scenario"]:t["tasks"] for t in T}
bad=0
for v in V:
    s=v.get("scenario"); i=v.get("task_idx")
    if s in taskmap and isinstance(i,int) and 0<=i<len(taskmap[s]):
        if v.get("task")!=taskmap[s][i]:
            bad+=1
            if bad<=10: print("TASK MISMATCH",s,i, repr(v.get("task"))[:100], "!=", repr(taskmap[s][i])[:100])
print("task text mismatches", bad)
# which keys not covered
keys_v=set((v.get("scenario"),v.get("task_idx")) for v in V)
missing=[(s,i) for s,ts in taskmap.items() for i in range(len(ts)) if (s,i) not in keys_v]
print("missing keys",len(missing), missing[:20])
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/awk/inspect.py

Possibly the duplicate with different code is a "corrupted" duplicate; the correct rule in the original dataset is one of them. The instruction: "Every original entry in the rule file must remain present and parseable, and a file that was wholesale-replaced, truncated, or corrupted makes the run ungradeable." So maybe we need to remove the wrong duplicate? But "Do not modify any evaluation, oracle, or verifier file" — conflicting. Yet "Every original entry in the rule file must remain present" means we should not remove entries. Hmm, maybe the defect isn't the duplicate; it's a bug in the selection in the bridge: e.g., `find_scenario_entry` uses normalized scenario names, and there could be scenario collisions after normalization (e.g., "e_commerce_33" vs "e-commerce-33")? Let's check normalization collisions. Also the scenario names may contain case/invalid chars. Let me check.

Actually, the phrase in the task "It selects, for each held-out episode, the rule the training bridge would select (by scenario and task index) from gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl in your repaired workspace" strongly suggests the verifier's behavior depends on the selection code (find_scenario_entry), and the commands expect us to fix selection or rules. And "do not modify any evaluation, oracle, or verifier file" might refer to not modifying held-out evaluation evidence under logs and the verifier code (awm/core/verify.py) — but bridge.py is training bridge, not "verifier"? Hmm.

The held-out evaluation evidence: val metrics (test_score over steps), logs/rollouts, idea_analysis. Let's look at the val score trajectory. The val stays ~0.35-0.39 while train success rises 0.2→0.47. That's a classic sign of reward hacking / wrong verifier, or overfitting. But note val/test score mismatch: test_score 0.3857 vs success_rate 0.390625 at step50; at 100: 0.3797 vs 0.390625; step150 0.3464 vs 0.3359. Hmm close.

But the "held-out evaluation evidence" is frozen; maybe there are more detailed evaluation files under logs? Only these. The verifier will replay episodes through rules. So it's about the verifier code correctness.

Let me examine the structure of gen_verifier entries and the env code. Maybe there's a systematic bug in the bridge's reward: `_shape_terminal_reward` etc. But that affects training reward, not held-out verifier replay. The verifier system "replays the episode through that rule" and classifies. It likely uses the same `run_verifier` semantics with the code rule. So if the rule returns "complete" incorrectly for many episodes, the held-out score suffers.

Let me inspect the data and logs. The 10 duplicate keys are suspicious: duplicates with differing code lengths could be where poisoned/incorrect rules were inserted. But the verifier selects the first one; keeping both is fine if first is correct? The instruction "Every original entry in the rule file must remain present and parseable" implies we shouldn't delete. But we may fix a duplicate if it's corrupt? Hmm.

Do not assume that an unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior." and "The system ... selects, for each held-out episode, the rule the training bridge would select (by scenario and task index) ... and replays the episode through that rule." So the repair must affect which rule is selected or the execution of the rule. Since rule file shouldn't be modified wholesale, maybe the defect is in `find_scenario_entry` — e.g., it matches by normalized scenario and returns the first entry. But the duplicate entries have identical scenario+task_idx, so no distinction. Unless one duplicate has task_idx as string "4" vs int 4, and find_scenario_entry compares `entry.get("task_idx") != task_idx`; if one is a string, it would be skipped. Let me check types. The printed repr showed task_idx= 4 (int). Hmm both int.

Maybe duplicates aren't the main defect but a red herring / planted "unusual" thing.

import json
import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple


_TOOL_CALL_PATTERN = re.compile(r"<tool_call>\s*(.*?)\s*</tool_call>", re.DOTALL)
_THINK_CLOSE = "</think>"


def _payload_after_think(action: str, require_think: bool) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the text that may contain a tool call / final answer.

    Tool-call extraction only looks after the first ``</think>``.  Content
    inside the reasoning block is ignored.  A missing close tag is a format
    failure when thinking is required.
    """
    close_idx = action.lower().find(_THINK_CLOSE)
    if close_idx == -1:
        if require_think:
            return None
        return action
    return action[close_idx + len(_THINK_CLOSE) :]


def awm_projection(actions: List[str], require_think: bool = False) -> Tuple[List[dict], List[int]]:
    """Parse the single MCP meta-tool call emitted by the AWM agent prompt.

    When thinking is enabled, an incomplete reasoning block is a format
    failure, just like malformed tool-call JSON.  Tool-call / final-answer
    parsing uses only the suffix after ``</think>``.
    """
    projected = []
    valid = []
    for action in actions:
        payload = _payload_after_think(action, require_think=require_think)
        if payload is None:
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
            continue
        matches = _TOOL_CALL_PATTERN.findall(payload)
        if not matches:
            content = payload.strip()
            projected.append({"name": "final", "content": content})
            valid.append(1 if content else 0)
            continue
        try:
            call = json.loads(matches[0])
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
            continue
        name = call.get("name", "") if isinstance(call, dict) else ""
        arguments = call.get("arguments") if isinstance(call, dict) else None
        if name not in {"list_tools", "call_tool"} or len(matches) != 1:
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
        else:
            projected.append({"name": name, "arguments": arguments})
            valid.append(1)
    return projected, valid

93	    """Generate the MCP server code and write it to a file.
94	
95	    Returns the path to the generated server code file.
96	    """
97	    envs = tools_jsonl_load(config.envs_load_path)
98	    envs = {normalize_scenario_name(e["scenario"]): e for e in envs}
99	    env = envs[config.scenario]
100	
101	    code = env["full_code"]
102	
103	    # Generated APIs should be safe to retry.  In particular, the mentoring
104	    # benchmark seeds the requested cohort in the initial database; a model
105	    # may therefore call create_program even though the row already exists.
106	    # The generated endpoint historically inserted blindly and surfaced the
107	    # UNIQUE(cohort_name) violation as an opaque MCP 500.  Make this endpoint
108	    # idempotent at generation time: return an existing row with the same
109	    # cohort name before attempting the insert.
110	    create_program_insert = (
111	        "    program = Program(cohort_name=body.cohort_name, start_date=start_date_obj, "
112	        "end_date=end_date_obj, target_audience=body.target_audience, "
113	        "max_participants=body.max_participants, created_by_user_id=CURRENT_USER_ID, "
114	        "created_at=now, updated_at=now)\n"
115	        "    session.add(program)"
116	    )
117	    create_program_idempotent = (
118	        "    existing = session.query(Program).filter(Program.cohort_name == body.cohort_name).first()\n"
119	        "    if existing is not None:\n"
120	        "        if (existing.start_date != start_date_obj or existing.end_date != end_date_obj "
121	        "or existing.target_audience != body.target_audience or existing.max_participants != body.max_participants):\n"
122	        "            session.close()\n"
123	        "            raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail='A program with this cohort_name already exists with different fields')\n"
124	        "        result = ProgramResponse(id=existing.id, cohort_name=existing.cohort_name, "
125	        "start_date_value=existing.start_date, end_date_value=existing.end_date, "
126	        "target_audience=existing.target_audience, max_participants=existing.max_participants, "
127	        "created_by_user_id=existing.created_by_user_id, created_at=existing.created_at, "
128	        "updated_at=existing.updated_at)\n"
129	        "        session.close()\n"
130	        "        return result\n"
131	        + create_program_insert
132	    )
133	    if create_program_insert in code:
134	        code = code.replace(create_program_insert, create_program_idempotent, 1)
135	
136	    # Vaccine definitions are keyed by name.  Tool-call retries currently
137	    # turn a successful first create into repeated UNIQUE(name) violations.
138	    vaccine_insert = (
139	        "    db_obj = VaccineDefinition(\n"
140	        "        name=vd.name,\n"
141	        "        species=vd.species,\n"
142	        "        description=vd.description,\n"
143	        "        created_at=datetime.utcnow(),\n"
144	        "        updated_at=None,\n"
145	        "    )\n"
146	        "    session.add(db_obj)"
147	    )
148	    vaccine_idempotent = (
149	        "    existing = session.query(VaccineDefinition).filter(VaccineDefinition.name == vd.name).first()\n"
150	        "    if existing is not None:\n"
151	        "        if existing.species != vd.species or (vd.description is not None and existing.description != vd.description):\n"
152	        "            session.close()\n"
153	        "            raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail='A vaccine definition with this name already exists with different fields')\n"
154	        "        resp = VaccineDefinitionResponse.from_orm(existing)\n"
155	        "        session.close()\n"
156	        "        return resp\n"
157	        + vaccine_insert
158	    )
159	    if vaccine_insert in code:
160	        code = code.replace(vaccine_insert, vaccine_idempotent, 1)
161	
162	    new_code = [
163	        'import warnings',
164	        'warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)',
165	        'from fastapi import HTTPException',
166	    ]
167	    for line in code.split("\n"):
168	
169	        if 'create_engine(' in line:
170	            left = line.split('create_engine(')[0]
171	            sql_path = f"'sqlite:///{db_path}'"
172	            right = f"create_engine({sql_path}, connect_args={{'check_same_thread': False}})"
173	            line = f"{left}{right}"
174	
175	        if 'uvicorn.run(app' in line:
176	            raw_code = f"""
177	            import os
178	            host = os.environ.get('HOST', '{config.host}')
179	            port = os.environ.get('PORT', {config.port})
180	            print(f'Server starting on port={{port}}')
181	            """
182	            lines = format_raw_code_to_lines(raw_code, indent=4)
183	            raw_code = f"""
184	            from fastapi_mcp import FastApiMCP
185	            mcp = FastApiMCP(app)
186	            mcp.mount_http()
187	            print("MCP server enabled, please visit http://{config.host}:{config.port}/mcp for the MCP service")
188	            """
189	            lines += format_raw_code_to_lines(raw_code, indent=4)
190	
191	            line = '    uvicorn.run(app, host=host, port=int(port))'
192	            new_code.extend(lines)
193	
194	        new_code.append(line)
195	
196	    server_code = "\n".join(new_code)
197	
198	    if config.temp_server_path is None:
199	        config.temp_server_path = os.path.join(
200	            os.path.dirname(config.envs_load_path),
201	            f"temp_server_{config.scenario.lower()}.py",
202	        )
203	
204	    with open(config.temp_server_path, "w") as f:
205	        f.write(server_code)
206	
207	    return config.temp_server_path
208

211	    output_dir = _prepare_server_dir(config)

213	    server_code_path = _generate_server_code(config, db_path)

229	    # After server exits, save final DB snapshot

233	        logger.info(f"Saved final database to {final_db_path}")
234	
235	    return ret

from dataclasses import dataclass
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
from datetime import datetime
from loguru import logger

from awm.tools import tools_jsonl_load, normalize_scenario_name
from awm.core.reset import reset_single_database

@dataclass
class Config:
    scenario: str
    envs_load_path: str # specify a path to load generated_envs.jsonl
    db_path: str | None = None # specify a path to load the database file, xxx.db
    host: str = "127.0.0.1"
    port: int = 8001
    temp_server_path: str | None = None # specify a temp server path, the code will be written to this path
    # Path to generated db schemas file (used when db_path is None to create DB from schema)
    db_schema_path: str = "./outputs/gen_db.jsonl"
    # Path to generated sample data file (used when db_path is None)
    sample_path: str = "./outputs/gen_sample.jsonl"
    # Output directory for server artifacts. Auto-created if not specified.
    output_dir: str | None = None

    def pre_process(self):
        self.scenario = normalize_scenario_name(self.scenario)
        assert os.path.exists(self.envs_load_path), f"Environment file {self.envs_load_path} not found"


def format_raw_code_to_lines(raw_code: str, indent: int) -> list[str]:
    no_indent_code = textwrap.dedent(raw_code).strip()
    indent_code = textwrap.indent(no_indent_code, ' ' * indent)
    return indent_code.split("\n")


def _prepare_server_dir(config: Config) -> str:
    """Prepare the server output directory.

    Creates outputs/servers/<timestamp>_<scenario> if output_dir is not set.
    Returns the output directory path.
    """
    if config.output_dir:
        output_dir = config.output_dir
    else:
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        output_dir = os.path.join("outputs", "servers", f"{timestamp}_{config.scenario}")
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    return output_dir


def _prepare_database(config: Config, output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Prepare the database for the server.

    If db_path is specified, uses it directly.
    Otherwise, creates a fresh DB via reset_single_database.
    Saves a copy as initial.db in the output directory.

    Returns the path to the working database file.
    """
    if config.db_path:
        db_file_path = config.db_path
        assert os.path.exists(db_file_path), f"Database file {db_file_path} not found"
        # Save initial DB snapshot
        initial_db_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "initial.db")
        shutil.copy2(db_file_path, initial_db_path)
        logger.info(f"Saved initial database to {initial_db_path}")
    else:
        # Create DB directly in output_dir as final.db (the working copy)
        db_file_path = reset_single_database(
            input_db=config.db_schema_path,
            input_sample=config.sample_path,
            scenario=config.scenario,
            database_dir=output_dir,
        )
        # reset_single_database names it <scenario>.db, rename to final.db
        final_db_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "final.db")
        os.rename(db_file_path, final_db_path)
        db_file_path = final_db_path
        logger.info(f"Created database at {db_file_path}")

        # Save initial DB snapshot (copy of the freshly created DB)
        initial_db_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "initial.db")
        shutil.copy2(db_file_path, initial_db_path)
        logger.info(f"Saved initial database to {initial_db_path}")

    return db_file_path


def _generate_server_code(config: Config, db_path: str) -> str:
    """Generate the MCP server code and write it to a file.

    Returns the path to the generated server code file.
    """
    envs = tools_jsonl_load(config.envs_load_path)
    envs = {normalize_scenario_name(e["scenario"]): e for e in envs}
    env = envs[config.scenario]

    code = env["full_code"]

    # Generated APIs should be safe to retry.  In particular, the mentoring
    # benchmark seeds the requested cohort in the initial database; a model
    # may therefore call create_program even though the row already exists.
    # The generated endpoint historically inserted blindly and surfaced the
    # UNIQUE(cohort_name) violation as an opaque MCP 500.  Make this endpoint
    # idempotent at generation time: return an existing row with the same
    # cohort name before attempting the insert.
    create_program_insert = (
        "    program = Program(cohort_name=body.cohort_name, start_date=start_date_obj, "
        "end_date=end_date_obj, target_audience=body.target_audience, "
        "max_participants=body.max_participants, created_by_user_id=CURRENT_USER_ID, "
        "created_at=now, updated_at=now)\n"
        "    session.add(program)"
    )
    create_program_idempotent = (
        "    existing = session.query(Program).filter(Program.cohort_name == body.cohort_name).first()\n"
        "    if existing is not None:\n"
        "        if (existing.start_date != start_date_obj or existing.end_date != end_date_obj "
        "or existing.target_audience != body.target_audience or existing.max_participants != body.max_participants):\n"
        "            session.close()\n"
        "            raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail='A program with this cohort_name already exists with different fields')\n"
        "        result = ProgramResponse(id=existing.id, cohort_name=existing.cohort_name, "
        "start_date_value=existing.start_date, end_date_value=existing.end_date, "
        "target_audience=existing.target_audience, max_participants=existing.max_participants, "
        "created_by_user_id=existing.created_by_user_id, created_at=existing.created_at, "
        "updated_at=existing.updated_at)\n"
        "        session.close()\n"
        "        return result\n"
        + create_program_insert
    )
    if create_program_insert in code:
        code = code.replace(create_program_insert, create_program_idempotent, 1)

    # Vaccine definitions are keyed by name.  Tool-call retries currently
    # turn a successful first create into repeated UNIQUE(name) violations.
    vaccine_insert = (
        "    db_obj = VaccineDefinition(\n"
        "        name=vd.name,\n"
        "        species=vd.species,\n"
        "        description=vd.description,\n"
        "        created_at=datetime.utcnow(),\n"
        "        updated_at=None,\n"
        "    )\n"
        "    session.add(db_obj)"
    )
    vaccine_idempotent = (
        "    existing = session.query(VaccineDefinition).filter(VaccineDefinition.name == vd.name).first()\n"
        "    if existing is not None:\n"
        "        if existing.species != vd.species or (vd.description is not None and existing.description != vd.description):\n"
        "            session.close()\n"
        "            raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail='A vaccine definition with this name already exists with different fields')\n"
        "        resp = VaccineDefinitionResponse.from_orm(existing)\n"
        "        session.close()\n"
        "        return resp\n"
        + vaccine_insert
    )
    if vaccine_insert in code:
        code = code.replace(vaccine_insert, vaccine_idempotent, 1)

    new_code = [
        'import warnings',
        'warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)',
        'from fastapi import HTTPException',
    ]
    for line in code.split("\n"):

        if 'create_engine(' in line:
            left = line.split('create_engine(')[0]
            sql_path = f"'sqlite:///{db_path}'"
            right = f"create_engine({sql_path}, connect_args={{'check_same_thread': False}})"
            line = f"{left}{right}"

        if 'uvicorn.run(app' in line:
            raw_code = f"""
            import os
            host = os.environ.get('HOST', '{config.host}')
            port = os.environ.get('PORT', {config.port})
            print(f'Server starting on port={{port}}')
            """
            lines = format_raw_code_to_lines(raw_code, indent=4)
            raw_code = f"""
            from fastapi_mcp import FastApiMCP
            mcp = FastApiMCP(app)
            mcp.mount_http()
            print("MCP server enabled, please visit http://{config.host}:{config.port}/mcp for the MCP service")
            """
            lines += format_raw_code_to_lines(raw_code, indent=4)

            line = '    uvicorn.run(app, host=host, port=int(port))'
            new_code.extend(lines)

        new_code.append(line)

    server_code = "\n".join(new_code)

    if config.temp_server_path is None:
        config.temp_server_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(config.envs_load_path),
            f"temp_server_{config.scenario.lower()}.py",
        )

    with open(config.temp_server_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(server_code)

    return config.temp_server_path


def run_server(config: Config):
    output_dir = _prepare_server_dir(config)
    db_path = _prepare_database(config, output_dir)
    server_code_path = _generate_server_code(config, db_path)

    # Save a copy of server code to output dir
    shutil.copy2(server_code_path, os.path.join(output_dir, "server_code.py"))

    logger.info(f"Server artifacts saved to {output_dir}")
    logger.info(f"Starting server for {config.scenario} on {config.host}:{config.port}")

    os.environ['PORT'] = str(config.port)
    os.environ['DATABASE_PATH'] = f"sqlite:///{db_path}"

    # Run server and capture log
    log_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "server.log")
    logger.info(f"Server log will be saved to {log_path}")
    ret = os.system(f"{sys.executable} {server_code_path} 2>&1 | tee {log_path}")

    # After server exits, save final DB snapshot
    final_db_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "final.db")
    if os.path.exists(db_path):
        shutil.copy2(db_path, final_db_path)
        logger.info(f"Saved final database to {final_db_path}")

    return ret


def start_server_process(
    scenario: str,
    envs_load_path: str,
    db_path: str,
    port: int,
    output_dir: str | None = None,
    temp_server_path: str | None = None,
) -> subprocess.Popen:
    """Start MCP server as a background subprocess.

    Returns the Popen handle so the caller can manage the process lifecycle.
    """
    cmd = [
        sys.executable, "-m", "awm.core.server",
        "--scenario", scenario,
        "--envs_load_path", envs_load_path,
        "--db_path", db_path,
        "--port", str(port),
    ]
    if output_dir:
        cmd.extend(["--output_dir", output_dir])
    if temp_server_path:
        cmd.extend(["--temp_server_path", temp_server_path])
    logger.info(f"Starting MCP server: {' '.join(cmd)}")
    return subprocess.Popen(
        cmd,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        start_new_session=True,
    )


def run(config: Config):
    run_server(config)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from simpleArgParser import parse_args
    config: Config = parse_args(Config)
    run(config)

91	        # MCP Tools

93	        You are in an MCP environment. Complete the user's task by calling MCP tools. You are already logged in; your user id is 1 when a tool requires it.
94	
95	        At each step, output at most one call using exactly this format:
96	        <tool_call>
97	        {"name":"list_tools","arguments":null}
98	        </tool_call>
99	
100	        The only top-level functions are `list_tools` and `call_tool`. Call `list_tools` exactly once at the beginning. To invoke an environment tool, use:
101	        <tool_call>
102	        {"name":"call_tool","arguments":{"tool_name":"mcp_tool_NAME","arguments":"{\\"arg\\":\\"value\\"}"}}

108	def parse_tool_calls(content: str) -> list[dict]:
109	    tool_calls = []
110	    pattern = r'<tool_call>\s*(.*?)\s*</tool_call>'
111	    matches = re.findall(pattern, content, re.DOTALL)
112	
113	    for i, match in enumerate(matches):
114	        data = tools_robust_json_loads(match.strip())
115	        if not data:
116	            logger.warning(f"Failed to parse tool call JSON: {match[:100]}")
117	            continue
118	
119	        # Handle list wrapping: [{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}]
120	        if isinstance(data, list):
121	            if len(data) > 0 and isinstance(data[0], dict):
122	                data = data[0]
123	            else:
124	                continue
125	
126	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
127	            continue
128	
129	        name = data.get("name", "")
130	        arguments = data.get("arguments", {})
131	
132	        if name.startswith("mcp_tool_"):
133	            arguments = {
134	                "tool_name": name,
135	                "arguments": arguments if arguments else {},
136	            }
137	            name = "call_tool"
138	
139	        tool_calls.append({
140	            "id": f"call_{int(time.time() * 1000)}_{i}",
141	            "name": name,
142	            "arguments": arguments,
143	        })
144	
145	    return tool_calls

173	def format_tools_for_response(tools: list[dict]) -> str:
174	
175	    def format_input_schema(schema: dict, indent_level: int = 6, parent_required: list | None = None) -> str:
176	        if not schema:
177	            return ""
178	
179	        result = ""
180	        indent_str = " " * indent_level
181	        properties = schema.get('properties', {})
182	        required_fields = parent_required if parent_required is not None else schema.get('required', [])
183	
184	        for prop_name, prop_info in properties.items():
185	            is_required = prop_name in required_fields
186	            required_str = " (required)" if is_required else " (optional)"
187	            prop_type = prop_info.get('type', 'unknown')
188	            description = prop_info.get('description', '')
189	            default = prop_info.get('default')
190	            enum_values = prop_info.get('enum')
191	            nested_properties = prop_info.get('properties', {})
192	            nested_required = prop_info.get('required', [])
193	
194	            result += f"{indent_str}- {prop_name}: {prop_type}{required_str}\n"
195	            if description:
196	                result += f"{indent_str}  Description: {description}\n"
197	            if default is not None:
198	                result += f"{indent_str}  Default: {default}\n"
199	            if enum_values:
200	                result += f"{indent_str}  Allowed values: {enum_values}\n"
201	
202	            if prop_type == "object" and nested_properties:
203	                result += f"{indent_str}  Properties:\n"
204	                nested_schema = {"properties": nested_properties, "required": nested_required}
205	                result += format_input_schema(nested_schema, indent_level + 4, nested_required)
206	
207	        return result
208	
209	    # filter out list_tools meta-tool
210	    actual_tools = [t for t in tools if t.get('name') != 'list_tools']
211	
212	    docs_text = f"Available MCP Tools ({len(actual_tools)} tools):\n"
213	    docs_text += "=" * 80 + "\n\n"
214	
215	    for i, tool in enumerate(actual_tools, 1):
216	        name = tool.get("name", "")
217	        description = tool.get("description", "")
218	        input_schema = tool.get("inputSchema", tool.get("input_schema", {}))
219	
220	        # add mcp_tool_ prefix
221	        mcp_name = f"mcp_tool_{name}" if not name.startswith("mcp_tool_") else name
222	
223	        # parse description for multi-line
224	        desc_lines = description.split('\n')
225	        first_line = desc_lines[0].strip() if desc_lines else "No description"
226	        more_desc = '\n'.join(line.strip() for line in desc_lines[1:]).strip() if len(desc_lines) > 1 else ""
227	
228	        docs_text += f"{i}. {mcp_name}\n"
229	        docs_text += f"   Description: {first_line}\n"
230	        if more_desc:
231	            for line in more_desc.split('\n'):
232	                if line.strip():
233	                    docs_text += f"   {line}\n"
234	
235	        if input_schema and input_schema.get('properties'):
236	            docs_text += f"   Parameters:\n"
237	            docs_text += format_input_schema(input_schema)
238	        else:
239	            docs_text += f"   Parameters: None\n"
240	
241	        docs_text += "\n"
242	
243	    return docs_text.strip()
